justification: Changes what the ledger asserts about three defects and lowers a build-blocking ratchet. It serves no number to a user, so not Critical — but closing a row on a wrong measurement would hide a live defect, and two of the three are closed on measurement alone.

falsifiable_check.command: python scripts/dq_probe_live.py --id DQ-24 && python scripts/dq_check.py && python -m pytest tests/test_dq_check.py -q
falsifiable_check.fails_when: DQ-24 exits 1 while any served Transport & Infrastructure provision lacks a v2_topic, so it cannot pass while the defect exists. dq_check goes red in the other direction on the two closures: DQ-25 and DQ-67 are now declared fixed, so if either turns out still to be broken the ledger contradicts itself. The cap test fails if _max_unverified_unresolved is left at 6 after the count drops to 3.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Observed at each step. DQ-24's probe exits 1 printing count=523 with its query — written before the row was given a check, so the row went from unmeasurable to red rather than to green. The cap test was watched failing too: leaving _max_unverified_unresolved at 6 after the count fell to 3 fails test_the_unverified_cap_matches_reality, which is the slack-detector added yesterday doing its job on its author. A third failure was real and useful: dropping why_no_check from the two closed rows tripped test_every_entry_declares_a_check_or_a_reason, so both now record why no standing probe is wanted.

pre_impl.existing_data: regulatory_provisions (Transport & Infrastructure SEPP: 2,909 current rows across TWO document ids), sepp_structured_requirements (560 rows, 553 with a NULL sepp_name). Read-only throughout — this change writes no database rows.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: DQ-24's document match assumes the SEPP can be identified by its document_id. It cannot be matched on 'Transport' alone: that also catches Penrith_DCP_2014__c10_transport_access_parking, a council DCP chapter. Verified the tightened pattern returns exactly the two SEPP document rows and nothing else. DQ-25's measurement assumes the owning SEPP is recoverable through provision_id — checked, because sepp_name is NULL on 553 of 560 rows and grouping by it is exactly what made the row look true.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No data written. Three ledger rows change status and one gains a probe; the two ratchet caps are lowered to the new real counts.
pre_impl.external_source_error: N/A — no network. The probe reads the live database through the shared read-only helper, which fails as UNKNOWN (exit 2) rather than clean when it cannot connect.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: None user-facing. The risk is internal: a row closed on a wrong measurement stops being watched. Both closures record the query behind them so a reader can re-run rather than trust.

functions.name: run
functions.input: a DQ id, looked up in the PROBES table where the new DQ-24 entry supplies a headline, parameterised SQL, its params tuple and the prose explaining a non-zero count
functions.output: an exit code plus the count printed WITH the query that produced it, so the row's status is generated by running rather than retyped — 0 only when the count is 0
functions.if_none: An unknown id is reported rather than treated as clean, and an unreachable database exits 2 (UNKNOWN), so 'could not measure' is never rendered as 'nothing wrong'.

values.value: the document_id LIKE pattern for the Transport & Infrastructure SEPP
values.guard_at: requires both 'Transport' and 'Infrastructure' and the year, verified to match exactly 2 document rows
values.if_missing: A looser pattern pulls in a Penrith DCP chapter and inflates the count with rows that have nothing to do with this defect.
Left at 6 while the count is 3, the ratchet would carry three rows of slack and the next unproven row would get in free. The test fails on exactly that.

queries.purpose: DQ-24: served Transport & Infrastructure provisions carrying no topic
queries.where_clause: document_id ILIKE '%Transport%Infrastructure%2021%' AND is_current AND v2_is_actionable AND v2_topic IS NULL
queries.if_zero: The row is declared open, so 0 makes the ledger ratchet go RED — correct, it would mean the tagging is done and the status is stale.
queries.if_wrong: Dropping v2_is_actionable would count 1,248 more rows nobody is served, making the number look four times worse than the exposure and moving for reasons no reader cares about.

break_it.scenario: DQ-25 is closed on a measurement that was itself wrong, so a live defect stops being watched.
break_it.what_happens: The table really is empty for that SEPP, the ledger says fixed, and nothing looks again.
break_it.how: The count was taken through the join that survives the NULL column (provision_id → regulatory_provisions.document_id) and cross-checked against the totals: 110 rows for that SEPP, 69 + 41 across its two document ids, the largest holding after Exempt and Complying Development. The closure records that query, so it can be re-run rather than trusted.
break_it.repro: SELECT count(*) FROM sepp_structured_requirements s JOIN regulatory_provisions p ON p.id = s.provision_id WHERE p.document_id ILIKE '%Transport%Infrastructure%2021%'

break_it.scenario: A GROUP BY sepp_name is used later and shows Transport as empty again, re-opening a closed row on a false reading.
break_it.what_happens: Work is redone chasing a defect that does not exist — which is how this row survived in the first place.
break_it.how: Both the ledger row and the why_no_check state plainly that 553 of 560 rows carry a NULL sepp_name and that the owning SEPP is only recoverable through provision_id. The trap is named where the next reader will be standing.
break_it.repro: SELECT sepp_name, count(*) FROM sepp_structured_requirements GROUP BY 1 — Transport is absent despite holding 110 rows

break_it.scenario: DQ-67 is closed while the precinct rules genuinely do matter.
break_it.what_happens: Town-specific numbers stay unextracted and unnoticed because the row that tracked them is gone.
break_it.how: Measured across all 21 precinct sections before closing: 13 carry zero numeric controls, the conservation block repeats identically in all three towns, and the single numeric precinct (Renwick) overlaps our served controls by about two values. What remains — is the right plan attached to the right address — is counted by DQ-66's probe, which is still open at 30. The row was folded, not dropped.

break_it.scenario: The Transport SEPP's duplicate document rows cause double counting or a half count.
break_it.what_happens: The number is wrong in either direction and the ratchet moves for the wrong reason.
break_it.how: The pattern deliberately spans both document ids rather than picking one, and the totals were checked against the per-document split (69 + 41 = 110 for the requirements side). The duplication itself is recorded in the ledger rows as a fact about this SEPP.
break_it.repro: SELECT DISTINCT document_id FROM regulatory_provisions WHERE document_id ILIKE '%Transport%Infrastructure%2021%'

break_it.scenario: A row is closed leaving neither a check nor a stated reason, so the ledger loses the thread entirely.
break_it.what_happens: A future reader sees 'fixed' with nothing behind it and no way to tell whether it was ever verified.
break_it.how: test_every_entry_declares_a_check_or_a_reason enforces one or the other. It caught this change in progress — both closures had their why_no_check removed and the test failed until each recorded why no standing probe is wanted.
